title: Supreme Court of India's SUVAS translation software: 36,271 judgments translated into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 other languages by 5 August 2024
summary: SUVAS, the Supreme Court of India's translation software, translated 36,271 Supreme Court judgments into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 languages by 5 August 2024
account: SUVAS (Supreme Court Vidhik Anuvaad Software) is the Supreme Court of India's artificial-intelligence-assisted tool for translating English judgments into Indian languages. The Supreme Court Observer had counted only 31 translated judgments from March 2020 to October 2021. The Hindu reported on 31 December 2023 that the e-SCR portal held 2,238 translated judgments in January 2023 and over 31,000 by the year's end. Officials credited the rise largely to retired High Court judges and law clerks who corrected the software's errors. A retired Madras High Court judge said that the Tamil translations he had seen could not be read. A 2025 peer-reviewed article cites Press Information Bureau figures as on 5 August 2024. By then 36,271 Supreme Court judgments were translated into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 other regional languages. The Supreme Court's Annual Report 2024–25 summarizes a judge's address that credits SUVAS with translating over 100,000 judgments into 18 regional languages. The report also records High Court translation work. The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, which the report says uses SUVAS, translated 4,426 Supreme Court judgments into Urdu. Manipur's AI-Assisted Legal Translation Committee translated 433 Supreme Court judgments into Meetei Mayek, of which 259 were uploaded and 174 were under review. The report calls this “AI-assisted translation” without naming the tool. These figures are aggregates. The sources give no single translated judgment with a dated delivery.
purpose: Translate Supreme Court and High Court judgments from English into Indian languages to widen access

No evaluation of use or comprehension by the public exists, and a retired judge told The Hindu that the Tamil translations cannot be read.

ai_role.statement: SUVAS produces machine drafts of the translations. Officials told The Hindu that the rise in output in 2023 came largely from retired High Court judges and their law clerks, who corrected the software's errors, and from review by the court's Editorial Section. The Supreme Court Observer counted only 31 translated judgments from March 2020 to October 2021, before this review system began. No source measures how much of the output or its accuracy the software itself provides.

data.retained_case_account: SUVAS (Supreme Court Vidhik Anuvaad Software) is the Supreme Court of India's AI-assisted tool for translating English judgments into Indian languages. A 2025 peer-reviewed article cites Press Information Bureau figures as on 5 August 2024. By then 36,271 Supreme Court judgments were translated into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 other regional languages. The Supreme Court's Annual Report 2024–25 summarizes a judge's address crediting SUVAS with translating over 100,000 judgments into 18 regional languages. It also records High Court translation work. Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, which the report says uses SUVAS, translated 4,426 Supreme Court judgments into Urdu. Manipur's AI-Assisted Legal Translation Committee translated 433 Supreme Court judgments into Meetei Mayek, 259 uploaded and 174 under review. The report calls this “AI-assisted translation” without naming the tool. These are aggregates. No single translated judgment with a dated delivery was found.

display.answer: The counts of 5 August 2024 come from the government's Press Information Bureau, and the 2025 Frontiers article repeats them. The figure of over 100,000 judgments comes from a judge's address that the Supreme Court's own annual report summarizes. The Hindu and the Supreme Court Observer counted the published translations themselves.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: SUVAS, the Supreme Court of India's translation software, translated 36,271 Supreme Court judgments into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 languages by 5 August 2024
fields.account: SUVAS (Supreme Court Vidhik Anuvaad Software) is the Supreme Court of India's artificial-intelligence-assisted tool for translating English judgments into Indian languages. The Supreme Court Observer had counted only 31 translated judgments from March 2020 to October 2021. The Hindu reported on 31 December 2023 that the e-SCR portal held 2,238 translated judgments in January 2023 and over 31,000 by the year's end. Officials credited the rise largely to retired High Court judges and law clerks who corrected the software's errors. A retired Madras High Court judge said that the Tamil translations he had seen could not be read. A 2025 peer-reviewed article cites Press Information Bureau figures as on 5 August 2024. By then 36,271 Supreme Court judgments were translated into Hindi and 17,142 into 16 other regional languages. The Supreme Court's Annual Report 2024–25 summarizes a judge's address that credits SUVAS with translating over 100,000 judgments into 18 regional languages. The report also records High Court translation work. The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, which the report says uses SUVAS, translated 4,426 Supreme Court judgments into Urdu. Manipur's AI-Assisted Legal Translation Committee translated 433 Supreme Court judgments into Meetei Mayek, of which 259 were uploaded and 174 were under review. The report calls this “AI-assisted translation” without naming the tool. These figures are aggregates. The sources give no single translated judgment with a dated delivery.
